notes: Ordered fail-fast chain, gated on REAL process exit codes only — never scraped stdout. A non-zero on ANY step fails QA and blocks the finish (verify-gate on Stop/SubagentStop).
1. tsc --noEmit: strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess repo-wide (test files, scripts, config, dead code) — 10-50x faster than a build.
2. eslint .: ESLint 9 flat config (eslint-config-next core-web-vitals + typescript). Next 16 removed `next lint` and `next build` no longer lints, so ESLint is its own step.
3. prettier --check .: single formatter; catches files not saved through the format-on-save hook. Never overlaps ESLint.

4. next build: the ONLY step that catches server/client boundary + RSC serialization errors (server-only imported into a client tree, non-serializable props across `use client`). Never set typescript.ignoreBuildErrors. Build happens EXACTLY ONCE here — Playwright's webServer runs `pnpm start` against this artifact, it does not rebuild.
5. drizzle-kit check: validates migration history integrity.

6. scripts/db-drift.sh: READ-ONLY drift guard — generates into a throwaway temp copy of the migrations dir and never mutates the tracked tree. Fails if schema.ts changed without a committed migration (the most common Drizzle prod incident).
7. vitest run: unit + SYNC components only. ASYNC React Server Components are UNSUPPORTED in Vitest — they are E2E-ONLY, proven via Playwright in step 8. Always `vitest run` (never watch).

8. playwright test: E2E against the PRODUCTION build from step 4 (webServer: `pnpm start`, reuseExistingServer: !CI, trace: on-first-retry). The only place async RSC behavior, rate-limit/cache behavior, and full boundary rendering are actually verified.
Order is load-bearing: cheapest and broadest checks first (tsc), the slow authoritative gate (next build) once, then tests against that single artifact.
`.format` is invoked by the format-on-save hook with the changed file path appended as the final argument (prettier --write --ignore-unknown <file>).
This chain is written by /quetrex-init into <repo>/.quetrex/verify.json; the ENGINE's verify-gate reads .verify[] verbatim and eval's each command string in the repo root.
